AUTOMATION_RISKS.HUMAN_RUBBER_STAMPING: Mitigation: human adjudication logged per candidate with reasons; approvals without reasons are invalid.
AUTOMATION_RISKS.LITERATURE_PRIOR_PULL: LLMs over-propose well-known effects (momentum, calendar anomalies). Allowed, but novelty critic labels literature-canonical proposals and the batch diversity quota limits them.
AUTOMATION_RISKS.MODE_COLLAPSE_AND_COSMETIC_NOVELTY: Mitigation: stratified quotas per family/source and a novelty critic that compares against consumed signatures.
AUTOMATION_RISKS.NO_TIMED_HUMAN_BASELINE: The 70-80% effort KPI has no measured historical baseline. The first shadow campaign must log human active minutes; any comparison to past sprints is labelled an estimate.
AUTOMATION_RISKS.OUTCOME_LEAKAGE_THROUGH_HUMAN_PROMPTS: Prompt authors know outcomes. Mitigation: prompts and few-shot examples go through the same scanner; few-shot examples are synthetic.

DATA_EXPANSION_DECISION.CHALLENGE_CONSIDERED: If most high-information proposals were impossible without new data, a generator run on current data would only show demand, not produce executable cards. This is acceptable for V0: Stream B exists to measure that demand, and Stream A still has executable ground in current datasets.
EVIDENCE: Past acquisitions were expensive and provenance-fragile when done ahead of a concrete card (funding/premium semantics remain unproven after two audits: B2-06, MARKET-04/04H).
When a concrete card needed data, a bounded acquisition was completed inside the card's feasibility unit (D13 panel, D11 calendar), so demand-driven acquisition is proven workable.

DECISION_RATIONALE: Generator V0 is evaluated on novelty, mechanism distance, falsifiability, data specificity and information gain, not on downstream positive rate. What it needs from history is coverage of mechanism regions, anti-rescue lineage, blocked-data examples and card-schema examples; 10 executed internal cards plus about 20 legacy H/B2/MARKET entries in structured memory supply those.

The history already contains every example class the critics must learn from: clean nulls in six distinct regions, prototypes, a replication that survived (D2 on BitMEX), statistical-but-not-practical structure (D13), and data/method blockers of four distinct kinds (D1 null-model mismatch, D6 source not pinned, D8 control support, B2-06/MARKET-04 publication-time semantics).

No named mechanism region is required for the generator evaluation to be valid. The one region previously named B-eligible (forward expectations / options) has zero executed cards, but a generator that proposes options mechanisms will route them to the data-blocked stream, where the data-gap ledger measures exactly how much distinct mechanism space options would unlock. Executing one options card first would not change whether the generator can be evaluated; it would spend a dataset acquisition before demand is measured.

The remaining weaknesses (prototype concentration in second-moment structure, D12 not replicated, no timed human-effort baseline) are about evidence strength and KPI measurement, not about whether generation can be automated. They are carried as explicit risks and measurement requirements.
